extra.message: Broken JWT Authentication - Signature Verification Disabled — Attacker can forge JWT tokens to impersonate any user (including admin), gaining access to all user passwords and bypassing any identity-based access controls throughout the application. [verified: get_identity() explicitly decodes JWT with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False at helpers.py:21, accepting any forged payload; resolve_me then sets this unverified identity into the request context, which resolve_password uses to grant admin access to all user passwords—no compensating control exists.]

JWT Decoded Without Signature Verification — Complete authentication bypass — attacker can impersonate any user, escalate to admin, and view all users' plaintext passwords [verified: Identical to finding [1]: get_identity at helpers.py:21 decodes tokens with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False, trusting the 'identity' claim without cryptographic proof; this identity controls password visibility in resolve_password and serves as the app's sole identity mechanism—no alternative verification exists.]

Plaintext Password Storage — All user passwords exposed if database is compromised; passwords visible to admins and via SQL injection [verified: Same plaintext password storage as finding [0] — the User model (models.py:14) stores passwords as-is and the Login/CreateUser mutations operate on raw passwords with no hashing, salting, or key derivation.]

Password Exposure via Identity Spoofing in resolve_password — Any attacker who forges an admin JWT token can dump all cleartext passwords from the database via a normal GraphQL query. [verified: Same as idx=28: resolve_password at views.py:61 returns cleartext for admin identity; JWT decoded without signature verification at helpers.py:21 allows identity forgery.]

Sensitive Data Exposure - Password Disclosure via Forged Identity — Complete exposure of all user passwords to an unauthenticated attacker who forges a JWT token. Leads to full account takeover of all users including admin. [verified: UserObject.resolve_password at views.py:62 returns cleartext password when context identity=='admin'; get_identity at helpers.py:21 decodes JWT with verify_signature=False, allowing any attacker to forge an admin token and dump all passwords.]

OS Command Injection + SSRF via ImportPaste mutation — Attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands AND make the server issue HTTP requests to internal/external services, read local files via file:// scheme, or attack internal infrastructure (SSRF), all without authentication. [verified: ImportPaste at views.py:211 constructs a URL from attacker-controlled scheme/host/port/path and passes it to os.popen via run_cmd; strip_dangerous_characters returns input unchanged in easy mode and only strips ; and & in hard mode, leaving backticks/$()/|/newlines exploitable.]

OS Command Injection via ImportPaste curl command — Remote code execution and SSRF — attacker can execute arbitrary commands and fetch internal resources [verified: Same as idx=3: ImportPaste passes attacker-controlled URL to os.popen via curl; strip_dangerous_characters is a no-op in easy mode and incomplete in hard mode.]

Plaintext Password Storage and Comparison — All user passwords are stored in plaintext and exposed if the database is compromised. SQL injection can directly extract all passwords. The weak seed credentials (admin:changeme) allow immediate privilege escalation. [verified: Same as idx=27: Login at views.py:233 compares plaintext passwords directly; passwords stored unhashed in models.py User model; seed credentials admin:changeme and operator:password123 in setup.py:64-65.]

Plaintext Password Storage — Complete exposure of all user passwords if database is compromised. Passwords visible to anyone with SQL injection access or database file access. [verified: Passwords stored as plaintext in User.password column (models.py:14) and compared directly in Login at views.py:234 via User.query.filter_by(username=username, password=password); no hashing (bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2) exists anywhere.]

Plaintext Password Comparison in Login — Passwords stored and compared in plaintext — any database compromise immediately yields all credentials; no protection against credential guessing or brute force attacks. [verified: Same as idx=27: Login at views.py:234 compares plaintext passwords directly against the database; passwords stored without hashing in models.py:14.]

SQL Injection via pastes filter parameter — Attacker can read, modify, or delete any data in the database including user credentials (passwords), paste contents, and audit logs; can potentially escalate to file read via SQLite load_extension or attach commands. [verified: resolve_pastes at views.py:320 interpolates user-controlled 'filter' directly into sqlalchemy.text() via % string formatting with zero sanitization; no middleware or validation intervenes on this path.]

OS Command Injection via systemDiagnostics cmd parameter — Attacker who can authenticate or guess admin credentials can execute arbitrary OS commands on the server. [verified: resolve_system_diagnostics requires admin auth (password 'changeme' seeded in setup.py:65) but allowed_cmds() returns True for any cmd in easy mode and the startswith check in hard mode fails to block shell metacharacters after allowed prefixes.]

OS Command Injection in systemDiagnostics resolver — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Flask process [verified: Same as idx=2: resolve_system_diagnostics passes cmd to os.popen with allowed_cmds returning True in easy mode; admin password 'changeme' is seeded and guessable.]

Weak Default Credentials for Admin and Operator Accounts — Trivial account takeover of admin and operator accounts. Admin access enables OS command execution and full server compromise. [verified: The weak_passwords list at setup.py:49 contains only 'changeme', making admin password trivially guessable; combined with plaintext storage, no rate limiting, and admin access enabling OS command execution, this is a direct path to full server compromise.]

Weak Default Credentials in Seed Data — Unauthorized access to admin and operator accounts using well-known default passwords [verified: random_password() at setup.py:49-50 always returns 'changeme' (single-element list) and operator password is literally 'password123' at line 64; plaintext storage, no brute-force protection on Login, and admin creds unlock OS command execution via resolve_system_diagnostics.]

Hardcoded Default Credentials for Admin and Operator Accounts — Anyone can log in as admin (password 'changeme') or operator (password 'password123') gaining access to system diagnostic commands and potentially OS command execution. [verified: Operator password 'password123' is literally hardcoded on setup.py:64 and admin password is effectively hardcoded as 'changeme' via single-element list at setup.py:49; both are stored plaintext, the unauthenticated /start_over endpoint resets the DB with these creds, and no rate limiting exists on Login — admin takeover yields OS command execution via systemDiagnostics.]

Hardcoded JWT Signing Secret — Anyone who knows the secret (it is in public source code) can forge valid JWT tokens for any user. [verified: app.config['JWT_SECRET_KEY'] = 'dvga' at app.py:15 is a hardcoded secret visible in public source code, used by flask_graphql_auth's create_access_token/create_refresh_token to sign JWTs; even though get_identity() in helpers.py:21 disables signature verification, the key itself is trivially known and enables token forgery on any deployment.]

Hardcoded Secret Keys — JWT and Flask Session — JWT tokens can be forged; Flask signed sessions can be tampered with; the 'env' cookie's integrity cannot be trusted; all cryptographic protections relying on these keys are defeated. [verified: Same hardcoded secrets at app.py:14-15 — SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY both set to 'dvga' in public source; the JWT key is actively consumed by flask_graphql_auth for token signing, and the Flask key (overriding the os.urandom assignment at line 10) compromises any Flask-signed data.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write via UploadPaste — Arbitrary file write anywhere on the filesystem — attacker can overwrite application code, templates, or system files [verified: Same vulnerability as finding [0]: save_file(filename, text) at line 23 calls open(WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename, 'w') at line 25 with no path sanitization; user-controlled filename from UploadPaste reaches this sink unchecked by any middleware, security function, or validation layer.]

Unrestricted File Upload via UploadPaste — Attackers can upload arbitrary files including malicious scripts, HTML files with XSS, or web shells to the server filesystem with no content validation. [verified: UploadPaste accepts user-controlled filename and content with no extension validation, MIME inspection, content-type checking, or size limits; combined with the unsanitized path concatenation in save_file (WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename), attackers can write executable scripts (.py, .html) to any writable directory—no upload validation exists in any middleware or security.py.]

GraphiQL Access Control Bypass via Cookie Manipulation — Unauthorized access to the GraphiQL interactive IDE in Expert mode, enabling schema exploration, query building, and easier exploitation of GraphQL vulnerabilities. [verified: IGQLProtectionMiddleware gates /graphiql solely on request.cookies.get('env')=='graphiql:enable' (middleware.py:122-124) with no signing/MAC; the value is trivially guessable from source and any client can set it. In Expert mode GraphiQL is fully blocked by the preceding is_level_hard() check (line 120), but an unauthenticated attacker can first switch to Beginner mode via the X-DVGA-MODE header (]

GraphiQL Access Bypass via Client-Manipulable Cookie — Attackers bypass the GraphiQL protection gate and gain access to the interactive GraphQL IDE, schema explorer, and the stack-trace-leaking error formatter. [verified: Same vulnerability as finding 0: the env cookie gate lacks integrity protection (no HMAC, Flask's SECRET_KEY='dvga' is hardcoded but unused for cookie signing here), and the value 'graphiql:enable' is publicly visible in the middleware source. An attacker trivially sets Cookie: env=graphiql:enable to bypass.]

Sensitive Data Leakage in Audit Log via Weak Token/Password Masking Regex — JWT tokens and passwords that don't match the exact expected format are stored in cleartext in the audit log and exposed to any anonymous user via the audits query. [verified: clean_query() regex matches only exact lowercase 'token:"..."' and 'password:"..."' patterns; any case/spacing/quote variation bypasses masking; the subscription path (models.py:47-52) stores raw query strings without calling clean_query() at all; resolve_audits (views.py:380) returns all audit entries unauthenticated.]

Weak OS Command Allowlist with Syntax Bug — The Expert mode command allowlist is ineffective. Attackers can still achieve code execution via echo with command substitution, and the 'whoami' restriction never applies due to the syntax bug. [verified: allowed_cmds() has implicit string concatenation ('ps' 'whoami' → 'pswhoami') breaking the intended 'whoami' restriction, and allows 'echo' which permits $() command substitution; strip_dangerous_characters() is never called on cmd in systemDiagnostics, so echo $(id) achieves OS command execution after authenticating with the known default password 'changeme'.]

IDOR / Missing Authorization in EditPaste mutation — Unauthorized modification of any user's pastes — attacker can alter or deface all pastes in the system [verified: Same as idx=4: EditPaste.mutate at views.py:142 updates paste by ID with no ownership verification; no authentication or authorization check exists.]

IDOR / Missing Authorization in DeletePaste mutation — Unauthorized deletion of any user's pastes — attacker can destroy all content in the system [verified: Same as idx=5: DeletePaste.mutate at views.py:163 deletes paste by ID with no ownership check; any anonymous caller can delete any paste.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via ImportPaste — Internal network scanning, cloud metadata service access, and exfiltration of internal resources [verified: SSRF aspect of idx=3: ImportPaste constructs a URL from attacker-controlled scheme/host/port/path and fetches it server-side via curl --insecure with no URL validation, enabling access to internal services and cloud metadata.]

Missing Authorization — WebSocket Subscription Leaks All Pastes — Any anonymous WebSocket client receives real-time broadcasts of all paste content including private pastes, enabling mass surveillance of all user activity. [verified: Same as idx=10: WebSocket /subscriptions at views.py:261 broadcasts all pastes via global_event with no authentication and no public/private filtering.]

IDOR / Missing Authorization — resolve_paste Returns Private Pastes Without Ownership Check — An attacker can enumerate paste IDs (integers) and read all private pastes in the system, accessing sensitive data intended to be visible only to the paste owner. No authentication or ownership verification is required. [verified: resolve_paste at core/views.py:325 filters only by id and burn=False with no ownership or public flag check; the Paste model has owner_id and public fields but neither is evaluated, and no middleware (core/middleware.py handles only depth/cost/introspection/denylist) nor before_request hook enforces access control on this resolver.]

Missing Authorization on readAndBurn - Burn-Once Paste Theft — Attacker can steal burn-once pastes meant for other users by guessing or enumerating paste IDs, defeating the single-use protection. [verified: resolve_read_and_burn at views.py:357 retrieves and deletes any burn-once paste by ID with no authentication or ownership verification; an attacker can enumerate IDs and steal burn-once pastes before intended recipients.]

Missing Authorization in deleteAllPastes Query — Mass deletion of all paste data by any unauthenticated attacker causing permanent data loss. [verified: Same as idx=21: resolve_delete_all_pastes at views.py:385 calls global Paste.query.delete() with no authentication or authorization.]

Missing Authentication on deleteAllPastes — Mass Data Destruction — Complete destruction of all paste data by any unauthenticated user [verified: resolve_delete_all_pastes at views.py:385 calls Paste.query.delete() with no authentication or authorization; any anonymous client can destroy all paste data.]

Missing Authentication on Database Reset Endpoint — Any unauthenticated attacker can wipe the entire database and reset the application to its default state at any time, causing persistent denial of service and data loss. [verified: Same as idx=40: /start_over at views.py:431-437 executes helpers.initialize() via os.popen to reset database with no authentication or CSRF protection.]

Unauthenticated Database Reset via /start_over — Any attacker can wipe the entire database (all users, pastes, audit logs) without authentication, causing permanent data loss and denial of service. [verified: /start_over at views.py:432 calls helpers.initialize() which runs 'python3 setup.py' via os.popen, resetting the entire database with no authentication, authorization, or CSRF protection.]

Server-Wide Security Downgrade via Unauthenticated X-DVGA-MODE Header — Attackers can globally disable all GraphQL security middleware by sending a single HTTP header, enabling batch attacks, deep recursion DoS, introspection, and other attacks that would otherwise be blocked in expert mode. [verified: Same as idx=9: before_request at views.py:468 reads X-DVGA-MODE header and disables all GraphQL security middleware globally without authentication.]

Unauthenticated Difficulty Mode Override Disables All Security — Global disabling of all GraphQL security middleware — attacker bypasses depth/cost/introspection/denylist/operation-name protections for all users [verified: Same as idx=9: X-DVGA-MODE header at views.py:470 allows unauthenticated global security downgrade, disabling all middleware.]

Security Middleware Bypass via X-DVGA-MODE HTTP Header — Attacker can trivially bypass all GraphQL security middleware by sending the X-DVGA-MODE: Beginner header, enabling introspection, deep recursion attacks, and accessing blocked operations regardless of global difficulty setting. [verified: The before_request handler at views.py:470 reads X-DVGA-MODE header and calls helpers.set_mode() with no authentication, disabling all GraphQL security middleware globally for any unauthenticated client.]

Missing Authentication on WebSocket Subscription Endpoint Leaking Private Paste Data in Real-Time — Unauthenticated attacker can connect to the WebSocket subscription endpoint and receive real-time notifications of all paste creations including private pastes and their full content, bypassing the public/private visibility model and enabling mass surveillance of all pastes created on the platform. [verified: Same WebSocket as idx=10: echo_socket at views.py:484 has no auth and Subscription resolver at views.py:261 broadcasts all pastes regardless of public/private flag via global_event.map(lambda i: i).]

Hardcoded Weak Operator Password in Database Seed — The operator account can be compromised using a publicly-known weak password; combined with plaintext storage, this is a reliable entry point for attackers. [verified: Operator password 'password123' is literally hardcoded at setup.py:64; operator cannot trigger OS commands (check_creds in security.py requires username=='admin') but still gains authenticated access to all pastes, audits, and mutations — trivially guessable, plaintext-stored, no rate limiting.]

Denial of Service via Excessive Recursion Limit — Attackers can crash the server by sending deeply nested or circular GraphQL queries that cause a stack overflow, resulting in denial of service. [verified: sys.setrecursionlimit(100000) at app.py:26 dramatically raises Python's recursion limit; in Easy mode the DepthProtectionMiddleware is bypassed (helpers.is_level_easy() returns True), so an attacker can send deeply nested or circular GraphQL queries that consume excessive stack memory and crash the server via stack overflow.]

GraphQL Introspection Enabled by Default — Attackers can discover the complete GraphQL schema including sensitive queries (systemDiagnostics, systemDebug, systemHealth) and mutations, significantly reducing the reconnaissance effort needed to exploit other vulnerabilities. [verified: IntrospectionMiddleware (middleware.py:109-115) explicitly passes through when is_level_easy() returns True, enabling full __schema introspection in Beginner mode. The mode is the default startup state and can be forced via the X-DVGA-MODE header bypass, so schema discovery is effectively always available to unauthenticated attackers.]

User Enumeration via CreateUser Mutation Error Messages — Attackers can enumerate valid usernames and email addresses by observing IntegrityError responses from the registration endpoint. [verified: CreateUser mutation (views.py) calls User.create_user() without try/except; SQLite IntegrityError from unique constraint violation on username/email propagates uncaught through Graphene to the client, revealing that the username or email already exists — enabling enumeration with no rate limiting.]

User Enumeration via Distinct Error Messages — Attackers can determine which usernames exist, enabling targeted password attacks [verified: check_creds() returns distinct messages ('Username is invalid' vs 'Password Incorrect') exposed directly via the unauthenticated systemDiagnostics resolver with no rate limiting, uniform error handling, or any compensating control.]

GraphQL Deny List Bypass via Operation Name Allowlist — An attacker can execute denied queries (such as systemHealth) in Expert/hardened mode by prefixing them with an allowed operation name like 'getPastes', completely circumventing the denylist protection mechanism. [verified: on_denylist() uses exact normalized-string matching while operation_name_allowed includes 'getPastes'; a query like 'query getPastes { systemHealth }' bypasses both checks because the normalized string 'querygetPastes{systemHealth}' matches neither denylist entry, confirmed by test_deny_list_expert_mode_bypass in test_vulnerabilities.py.]

Stack Trace and Internal Path Disclosure in Error Responses — Attackers learn internal file paths, application structure, and gain debugging context that aids in crafting more sophisticated attacks. [verified: Same function and same reachable /graphiql endpoint as findings [0] and [1]; the guard excludes only the 'GraphiQL Access Rejected' message, so any other GraphQL error triggered via /graphiql returns full tracebacks and file paths in the extensions.exception object.]

User Enumeration via Unhandled IntegrityError in CreateUser Mutation — Attacker can enumerate all registered usernames and email addresses by observing whether CreateUser returns an IntegrityError (account exists) or succeeds (account created), facilitating targeted password attacks and privacy violations. [verified: CreateUser at views.py:98 calls User.create_user() without try/except; duplicate username/email triggers an unhandled IntegrityError from db.session.commit() in models.py:18 that propagates with stack trace details via format_custom_error.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Brute-force password guessing against user accounts, credential stuffing, and Denial of Service via mass account creation. [verified: Same as idx=7: Login mutation at views.py:225 and CreateUser at views.py:92 lack any rate limiting, account lockout, or throttling.]

Denial of Service via Resource-Intensive systemUpdate Query — Server thread pool exhaustion. Legitimate users cannot access the application while the attack is ongoing. [verified: resolve_system_update at views.py:333 calls security.simulate_load() which blocks the thread for up to ~50 seconds per request with no rate limiting; repeated queries exhaust the server thread pool.]

Insecure Cookie Without Security Flags — The env cookie controlling GraphiQL access can be intercepted over unencrypted connections, read by XSS attacks, and manipulated via CSRF to bypass the GraphiQL protection middleware. [verified: Same as idx=11: resp.set_cookie('env', 'graphiql:disable') at views.py:394-395 omits Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags on the GraphiQL access-control cookie.]

Audit Log Exposure Without Authentication — Exposure of all GraphQL operations performed by all users. Attackers can learn the schema, discover valid queries, and extract sensitive data from audit entries that the cleanup regex missed. [verified: /audit route at views.py:427 and resolve_audits at views.py:380 return all Audit entries with no authentication; clean_query regex in models.py:25 is best-effort masking that fails on non-standard formatting.]

CSRF on State-Changing GET Routes (difficulty change and database reset) — Attacker can force a victim to change the global difficulty level (disabling security middleware) or wipe the entire database by tricking them into visiting a crafted link. [verified: /start_over at views.py:431 and /difficulty/<level> at views.py:441 are state-changing GET endpoints with no CSRF tokens or origin validation; Flask has no CSRF protection configured.]

CSRF on State-Changing GET Routes — An attacker can forge cross-site requests to reset the database or change the difficulty mode by tricking an authenticated administrator into visiting a malicious page. [verified: Same as idx=8: /start_over at views.py:431-434 and /difficulty/<level> at views.py:441 are state-changing GET endpoints with no CSRF tokens or origin validation.]

Denial of Service via systemUpdate — Unbounded Resource Consumption — Attackers can exhaust server resources (CPU/thread pool) by sending multiple concurrent systemUpdate queries, causing denial of service for legitimate users. [verified: simulate_load() sleeps for 20-50 seconds per request with no rate limiting or authentication; while gevent cooperative scheduling mitigates thread exhaustion, concurrent requests can still saturate the connection pool and degrade availability.]
